name: codex
title: Codex / GPT cross-vendor interface
summary: Adds the OpenAI-backed half of the harness: the Sol reviewer as the default cross-family reviewer for Claude-authored campaign work through the Codex CLI, a two-rung exceptional-order-only executor lane through the same CLI (Sol at high, GPT-6 Astra at xhigh), and the two-architect /cross-compare-plan session (independent drafts, cross-critique, blind synthesis) whose GPT lane (Sol, high effort) runs read-only through the same CLI.

bin: codex (Codex CLI) — for reviewer-codex, executor-codex-heavy, executor-codex-principal, and the cross-compare architect lane
env: OPENAI_API_KEY or `codex login` — review, execution, and cross-compare

notes: reviewer-codex is the default independent reviewer for Claude-authored campaign work; Codex-authored work goes to fresh-context Opus review instead. There is no reviewEngine switch. Docs-only work is exempt: a prose-only diff routes to fresh-context Opus review — no cross-family requirement, no alarm.

The Codex executor lane has two rungs, both exceptional-only and both a Director routing decision made at PLAN time — never routine work. executor-codex-heavy (GPT-5.6 Sol, high) is the default rung, for a problem with concrete prior evidence that Anthropic models struggled on it. executor-codex-principal (GPT-6 Astra, xhigh) is the rung above it, for an order that has already bounced at the heavy rung or whose shape is long-horizon agentic work in a live terminal. Astra is priced well above Sol per token, so the rung earns its place only where the extra depth changes the outcome. The Claude executors remain the default path for everything else.

Config keys (.claude/orchestra.json under "codex"): reviewModel (default gpt-5.6-sol), reviewTimeoutMs (default 2700000), execHeavyModel (default gpt-5.6-sol), execHeavyEffort (default high), execPrincipalModel (default gpt-6-astra), execPrincipalEffort (default xhigh), crossplanModel (default gpt-5.6-sol), crossplanEffort (default high). Each executor rung reads only its own pair, so pinning one never moves the other; the heavy keys keep the names they shipped with.

Windows: codex-command-runner.exe, codex-resources AND codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe must sit DIRECTLY beside codex.exe. Codex resolves the sandbox helper by name, so a copy one directory down (inside codex-resources\) is never found — the sandbox is never set up and BOTH lanes (review and execution, at either rung) return nothing while looking healthy. The self-check below finds that state and repairs it where it can.
Without this pack the harness still gets full fresh-context Opus review and Claude execution; it just has no cross-vendor option.
